result:
My final answer is in `final.py`. It scores **0.5624 on the search split** against the LRU baseline's 0.365, and I used **14 of the 24 scorer calls**. The log counts 14; I ran the scorer 15 times, because one call was rejected as invalid and wasn't logged.

| trace | hit rate |
|---|---|
| hot_with_scans | 0.248 |
| loop_and_hot | 0.657 |
| phases | 0.647 |
| mixed | 0.263 |
| recency | 0.847 |
| shifting_loops | 0.713 |

**How it works:** the base policy is W-TinyLFU. New keys go into a small recently-used area. When that area is full, a key only moves into the main cache if it has been requested more often than the main-cache key it would push out. This keeps one-off scans and loops longer than the cache from flushing out keys that are requested often. The main cache keeps a protected section for keys that have been hit more than once.

**What changes per trace:** the best settings differ by access pattern, so the cache runs 17 copies of itself in the background. Each copy tries a different combination of three settings:
- the size of the recently-used area, from 1% to 99% of capacity;
- how quickly old request counts fade;
- the size of the protected section.

Each copy only tracks which keys it would hold; the real cache stores nothing for them. The real cache switches to the settings of whichever copy has had the most recent hits. It only switches when the lead is clear, so it doesn't flip back and forth on noise. This let one design do well on traces where plain LRU was best (recency) and on traces where a frequency filter was best (loops).

**Things to know:**
- **Runtime:** a full scorer run took about 2.5 s, against the 8 s limit. That leaves roughly a 3× margin, but a heavily loaded laptop would eat into it.
- **Risk on unseen traces:** I tuned mostly on synthetic traces I generated locally and used the scorer only to confirm the main choices. The last few settings I tried moved the score by less than 0.005, which is probably noise, so I stopped there rather than fit the search traces more closely.

The working candidates and my local test scripts are in the `c/` folder there.
